title: Michael Jordan: The Life
author: Roland Lazenby
target_audience: Readers interested in biographies of influential figures
Anyone studying leadership, excellence, or sports history
core_themes: The making of an athletic icon
The influence of family and upbringing
The business of sports and global branding
primary_purpose: To provide a comprehensive and nuanced portrait of Michael Jordan, going beyond his public persona to explore his upbringing, psychology, career, and impact on basketball and global culture.

structure_format.narrative_style: In-depth, journalistic, and richly detailed with extensive interviews
structure_format.organization: Chronological, beginning with Jordan's family heritage, childhood, through his basketball career and post-retirement
features: Extensive interviews with friends, family, teammates, and rivals
Insightful analysis of character and motivation

key_concepts_lessons: Extraordinary achievement often comes from a combination of talent, work ethic, and intense competitiveness.
Family history and early environment shape personal drive and ambition.
Even legends have flaws; Jordan’s relentless pursuit of greatness sometimes led to personal conflicts and controversy.
Race, social context, and American culture played significant roles in Jordan’s life and career.
The story of Michael Jordan is also the story of the globalization of basketball and the rise of the sports marketing industry.
notable_features: Draws on hundreds of interviews and years of research
Presents a multi-dimensional portrait—athlete, businessman, competitor, and public figure
Contextualizes Jordan’s story within American culture and the evolution of the NBA
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2014, at a time when Michael Jordan’s legacy was well-established, the book capitalizes on decades of public fascination, the evolution of the NBA, and changing discussions about race and celebrity in America.
reception_impact: Received critical acclaim for its depth and honesty
Regarded as an authoritative biography of Michael Jordan
Praised for shedding light on lesser-known aspects of Jordan’s life
Some reviewers noted its length and detail might be overwhelming for casual fans
comparable_titles: Playing for Keeps: Michael Jordan and the World He Made by David Halberstam
Eleven Rings: The Soul of Success by Phil Jackson
The Jordan Rules by Sam Smith
Mamba Mentality: How I Play by Kobe Bryant
